title: What I keep noticing
dek: PointCast opens a warm, visual weekly about rituals, towns, networks, useful knowledge, and the agreements that let people live together
body:
Everything PointCast wants to write about keeps turning out to be the same subject. Coffee is a ritual for coordinating a body with a morning. A library is a protocol for coordinating a town with its own memory. Animal Crossing is a gift economy with better graphics than most gift economies. A mesh network is a neighborhood deciding it can be its own utility. Even LaCroix—especially LaCroix—is a story about how desire gets manufactured, distributed, and shelved.

What I Keep Noticing is the editorial front door for that beat. Five private desks—Ritual, Coordination, Study Of, Utility, and Place—keep the calendar balanced. Readers travel by altitude instead: Body, Home, Town, Network, and World. One story can cross several at once, because none of these subjects stay in their assigned section for long.

The first planned run is six August pieces anchored by The Future of the Library, with Why LaCroix, Animal Crossing Is a Gift Economy, How to Calendar a Life, Places We Said to Visit in 2023, and a practical town mesh-network case study. New Friday. Field notes arrive between.
